subject: Nightly batch surge caused VPC throughput collapse — urgent tuning + exec sync
raw:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Cole <rachel.cole@medlinecorp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly batch surge caused VPC throughput collapse — urgent tuning + exec sync

Hi Rachel / team,

We observed a major throughput collapse in your VPC during the 02:00 nightly inference batch (US-West). Around 02:03 the cluster entered a sustained backpressure state for ~28 minutes: per-customer concurrency fell from expected 1.2k qps to ~120 qps, p95 generation latency spiked from 320ms to ~2.9s, and we saw a 12% error rate (mostly 503/504 timeout and kernel OOM retries). Ops attached the abbreviated logs (hotrod-logs-20261105.tar.gz.txt) and a k8s describe.

Initial observations:
- The batch window contains a new payload pattern (large multi-turn prompts with long decode lengths) that increased KV cache pressure and broke our prefix coalescing assumptions.
- Several pods reported small GC-like stalls in the runtime while migrating quantized tensors; these coincide with high CPU steal on the node (see k8s-describe-medline-ns.txt).
- Autoscaler behaved as configured but the additional nodes were slow to register ready due to an image-pull hotspot in the subnet.

Immediate asks:
1) Can MedLine provide the job that triggers the nightly multi-turn payloads (we included sample-payloads.json).
2) We need a ~30 minute call with your ops lead + our on-call infra to walk through logs and authorize a temporary fallback route to our hosted pool for 10% of the nightly batch while we tune.
3) Please confirm whether a short maintenance window tonight at 23:30 PST is possible for kernel-level runtime toggles (low-risk).

I'm looping Vanessa and David to propose mitigations. This is elevated to me as a potential executive briefing item if we cannot restore expected throughput and SLA baseline by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Nightly batch surge caused VPC throughput collapse — urgent tuning + exec sync

Team — quick internal readout before the call:

Summary of proposed mitigations (short-term -> medium-term):
1) Short-term (0–4 hours):
   - Add a temporary routing policy that directs 8–12% of traffic for etl/batch-infer/medline-nightly to a pooled hosted cluster that has pre-warmed KV caches for similar prompt shapes. This is a low-risk fallback and reduces pressure on the VPC.
   - Apply a conservative decode-length cap on the nightly job at the ingress proxy (we can set 1024 tokens) to reduce worst-case KV pressure.
   - Increase pod CPU reservation on hot nodes to avoid runtime stalls; we can do this as a patch without a full maintenance window.

2) Medium-term (24–72 hours):
   - Tune the runtime kernel selection to prefer asynchronous dispatch for the affected model variant (we think quantized attention scheduling is tripping on certain sequence lengths). Priyom will own the kernel tuning track.
   - Add a small canary rollout of the tuned runtime into one availability zone to verify no regressions.
   - Patch the autoscaler to prefer warm pool rehydration by pre-pulling images into standby nodes (work with MedLine infra).

Risks: routing to hosted adds cost and slightly different tail behavior; decode cap can change output quality for that pipeline (we should run a quick sample evaluation).

I'll stand up the bridge in 15 unless Rachel requests otherwise. Priyom — can you confirm availability for the kernel work?

David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Team and MedLine execs,

Thanks to everyone who joined the diagnostic bridge. Quick recap and exec-level ask so we have a single action tracker for leadership:

What happened:
- Last night's nightly batch introduced larger-than-expected multi-document prompts. This increased sequence length variance and KV cache churn, which combined with image-pull delays and a hot node kernel stall to produce a sustained throughput collapse (~90% drop for 28m).

Impact:
- SLA exposure: estimated customer p95 SLA breach window = 00:59–01:27 PST; approximate revenue risk (est.) = $4.7k incremental lost revenue and support credits if not remediated within 48h.
- Customer impact: several downstream pipelines slowed; MedLine ops paged and issued a partial rollback for one job.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA):
1) Apply ingress decode cap at 1024 tokens for etl/batch-infer/medline-nightly (Owner: MedLine infra + Redwood routing team) — ETA: 2 hours.
2) Enable 10% hosted fallback for tonight's window as a mitigation (Owner: Redwood routing + MedLine sign-off) — ETA: 3 hours.
3) Priyom: begin kernel tuning work and prepare a canary build (Owner: Priyom Das) — ETA: 48h for canary candidate.
4) David: prepare post-mortem with timeline and recommended autoscaler pre-pull patch (Owner: David Kim) — ETA: 72h.

Exec ask: Rachel / Antonio, please confirm by 18:00 PST today whether MedLine will approve the 10% hosted fallback for tonight. If not approved, we will still proceed with ingress caps and node reservation changes but will need a short maintenance window tomorrow 01:00–01:15 PST for the more invasive runtime toggle.

I'll draft the exec summary for both sides once we have sign-off.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
